methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Neuromeka is a public-stage robotics and manufacturing company (KOSDAQ listing, ticker 277810.KQ) that has raised $36.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of nine peers: one public company and eight private robotics firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this valuation. While ten same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, none satisfy the filtering criteria for stage and valuation-tier alignment required for reliable triangulation. Specifically, zero same-stage peers, zero adjacent-stage peers, and zero similar-tier peers were identified. Applying an all-sector median would introduce substantial methodological error by including fundamentally misaligned comparables. The narrow public peer set (n=1) and fragmented private cohort preclude robust statistical benchmarking.

Given the inapplicability of standard peer triangulation, this valuation cannot be supported by the available quantitative methods and data. A defensible range would require either: expansion of the comp set with stage- and tier-aligned peers; application of alternative methods such as DCF or precedent transaction analysis; or disclosure of market transaction data from Neuromeka's public listing. The core uncertainty is the absence of sufficient comparable evidence to anchor valuation within a credible range.
